# ANTIGRAVITY

Intelligence for work that happens in the physical world.Designed by operators, not observers.

Book a callSee Mise Company / Product / Horizon Enter the system In build Mise, Product 01 for kitchens In research Construction, back office and project marketplace Defined Mechanics, back office, job marketplace, and vehicle data

The company

## Real work is still done by people with their hands.

Computers keep getting smarter. We build software that helps them do it better: cooking, building, fixing.

We watch how the work really happens. Then we turn it into clear steps and clear choices. And a person always makes the final call. Every day of real work also teaches us how the work is done. One day, that knowledge is how machines will learn physical work too.

But physical work is still unmeasured where it happens. Software knows what was sold and what was ordered. It does not know what was used, what was wasted, or what hands actually did. That gap wastes money and scarce labour every day. So we build physical AI setups inside real operations, kitchens first, to capture that truth and create production data that teaches machines how humans work.

Kitchens

Food prepared, food sold, and food wasted are three different numbers in most kitchens, and only one of them is in the system.

A figure joins this card only with a named, filed source.

Construction

What was contracted, what is claimed complete, what is accepted complete, and what is approved to pay are four different states, and most projects track them as one.

A figure joins this card only with a named, filed source.

Mechanics

A vehicle knows a great deal about its own fault. Most of that record never reaches the job log, the estimate, or the parts list in a usable form.

A figure joins this card only with a named, filed source.

How we build it

## Each step funds the next, and feeds it.

We do not start with a robot and look for work for it. We start with the work, earn the right to be inside it, learn it from the inside, and only then give that learning a body.

01

### Sell the service

Back office plus service marketplace for physical businesses.

What we sell or build

For kitchens, Mise. For construction and mechanics, the same pattern in their language, a back office that runs the job and a marketplace where work and specialists are posted and hired by availability and calendar.

What it produces

Revenue, real jobs running on our system, and a trusted place inside the operation.

What it makes possible next

A real operation that will let us measure the work from inside, with consent, as part of a service it already values.

02

### Capture inside the work

A universal capture kit, the same in every trade.

What we sell or build

Sensors and cameras built into things workers already wear and rooms they already work in, sold or placed through partners to better the service. Direction only today, this kit is not built yet, and the site must say so wherever the kit is described as a product.

What it produces

Primary data, a linked record of a real job, what hands did, what was used, in what order, and what the outcome was.

What it makes possible next

A dataset no lab study and no outside dataset contains, commercial physical work captured from inside.

03

### Compare with the world

Primary data checked against secondary data, in one common form.

What we sell or build

A single representation for physical work, so kitchen, construction, and mechanic episodes can be compared and trained together without rebuilding the format per trade. Our research name for the current draft of that format is the Physical Work Episode, described in plain language on the research log.

What it produces

A clear map of where real work differs from lab and public data, and where outside data can be trusted.

What it makes possible next

Training that starts from truth about real work, not only from clean examples.

04

### Train one brain

One brain that learns across jobs and across trades.

What we sell or build

A small brain first, tested on narrow, measured tasks, then widened only where the results pass. Research in progress today, no trained general brain is claimed on this site.

What it produces

Skills that transfer, grasping, tool use, sequencing, and recovery from errors, learned from many jobs, not one demonstration.

What it makes possible next

Intelligence that a body can use, tested back in real jobs, not only in a lab.

05

### Give it a body

Partner for a body first, ship our own when the economics hold.

What we sell or build

A partnership with a mechatronics company that already builds a capable body, or, when the money and the results are there, our own robots, placed into the same trades we already serve.

What it produces

One general purpose robot that can work across the jobs it was trained inside.

What it makes possible next

Every new trade we enter becomes a new skill for robots already placed, which makes each placed robot more valuable over time.

The Antigravity staircase: service first, capture inside the work, comparison with the world, one brain, then a body. Each step is a business on its own and the training ground for the next.

Product 01 Mise

## Software that runs the back of a kitchen.

Mise keeps one true list of your recipes. Every sale works out which ingredients it used. When stock runs low, Mise writes the order. A person approves it before anything is bought. Mise is the first place we prove this works. It is not the whole company.

Method

## Built by watching real work.

01

### Measure before we claim.

A headline with no evidence under it does not ship, on this site or in a product.

02

### Inside, not outside.

A physical business is not a rock to watch. It is like a cell, inside the membrane is a whole working system. We build from inside that system.

03

### The person stays in charge.

Our systems show evidence and propose. A person approves what is sent, ordered, accepted, or paid.

04

### Stage honestly.

In build means in build. In research means in research. Defined means defined, not launched.

Concept visual · Two hands, one joint

Step 2, direction

## One kit in every trade, so the data speaks one language.

If the kit changes per industry, the data format changes per industry, and one brain can never learn across trades. So the kit is designed to be universal. The clothes change, a kitchen mask, construction safety glasses, a mechanic work shirt. The sensors and the data points stay the same.

Sensor shirt

Torso movement, posture, and effort across a shift

Glasses or mask camera

What the worker sees, head movement, and voice. In a kitchen this sits in a mask workers already wear, so no new habit is needed

Sensor gloves

Hand and finger movement, grip, touch, and how long a hand holds a tool or material. Hands are where skilled work lives

Overhead camera

Full body movement in the space

Room camera

The whole scene, other people, objects moving, and the state of the room around the work

The business record

Order, invoice, job log, estimate, parts, and outcome, linked to the same episode, so the movement is never separated from its result

Concept visual · The capture kit, one case

Concept visual · The recorder

Concept visual · Glasses that see the work

Concept visual · The sensor shirt

The capture kit is a design direction, not a built product. No kit is for sale, no capture is running in a customer site today, and the final sensor set will be set by experiment results, not fixed in advance on this page.

The asset

## Lab data teaches clean examples. Real jobs teach the work.

Public and lab datasets are useful, and we use them. They are also, by design, clean, short, and separated from money and outcomes. A real commercial job is none of those things. The gap between the two is not a problem to hide. Measured properly, that gap is the asset.

| Topic | In secondary data | In primary data from a real job |

| Task | An isolated activity, filmed to be studied | A full job, with preparation, interruptions, and a customer waiting |

| Sequence | Steps in a tidy order | The real order, including rework, waiting, and fixes |

| Failure | Rare, and often removed | Stockouts, faults, rework, and mistakes, with what fixed them |

| Outcome | A label given by a researcher | Sold, accepted, paid, wasted, or redone, from the business record |

| Hands and tools | Often visible, rarely measured with force or contact | Gloves, tools, and materials measured together, by design of the kit |

| Consent and rights | Set by the dataset licence, which may bar commercial use | Set by our customer and worker agreements, designed for training use from the start |

Not all public data can be used to build a commercial product. Some respected datasets are non commercial only, and some licences are drafts, not permission. We treat licence checks as a gate before any dataset is used, and our research log names the status of the datasets we rely on.

### What an episode count would mean, as a planning model

Model100 episodes

Enough to test whether our format holds real work at all

Model1,000 episodes

Enough to compare real work with lab work trade by trade

Model10,000 episodes

Enough to train skills that must survive variation between sites

These are planning thresholds for our own experiments, not results and not a dataset we hold today. The research that sets the real thresholds is in progress and will be published in the research log when it is graded.

Pause sequence

The horizon

## Earth is the training ground.

A machine sent far from Earth cannot count on perfect conditions or a fixed script. It will need what people know: how to cook, build, and repair. And what to do when things go wrong.

The end goal is autonomy for physical work: machines that can cook, make, and build reliably anywhere, even beyond Earth.

“When robots land on Mars, someone has to teach them to cook. We’re writing the cookbook.”

## Privacy

×

Last updated 30 October 2026Website privacy noticeVersion 1.2

This notice explains what happens to information when you visit this website or contact Antigravity Analytics Private Limited.

### 1. Who is responsible

Antigravity Analytics Private Limited is responsible for the information it receives through this website and through messages sent to its published email addresses.

### 2. Information involved

- Technical delivery data: IP address, browser and device details, request time, requested file, referring page and basic security logs may be processed by the site host to deliver and protect the website.

- Correspondence: if you email us, we receive the address you use, the contents of your message and any attachments you choose to send.

- Website preferences: this build does not create a first-party account, profile or persistent preference record.

### 3. Why information is used

Technical data is used to deliver the site, maintain security, diagnose faults and understand aggregate demand. Correspondence is used to answer the purpose of your message, evaluate a partnership or investment conversation, and keep a necessary business record.

### 4. Analytics programme

Antigravity uses Simple Analytics to understand aggregate page views, broad traffic sources and anonymous interaction events (section views, button and link clicks). The purpose is to improve the clarity, accessibility and reliability of the site, not to build advertising profiles. Simple Analytics sets no cookies, collects no personal data, and honours Do Not Track.

Advertising measurement is also present, and it runs only with your consent. If you accept in the cookie banner, the Meta Pixel loads on this site. It records page views, form submissions and booking link clicks, sets cookies, and shares device, browser and interaction data with Meta so Antigravity can measure campaign performance and show ads to people who visited this site. If you decline, the pixel does not load and nothing is sent to Meta by this site. No TikTok pixel is installed on this site. Your choice is stored in your browser local storage, and you can change it at any time from the Cookies section of this page. Advertising measurement will not capture message contents, keystrokes, clipboard contents, precise location, identity documents, sensitive attributes or screen recordings.

### 5. Sharing

Information may be handled by infrastructure and email providers acting for Antigravity, or disclosed where required by law. It is not sold as a personal-data list. We do not use this website to collect payment-card details, government identifiers or sensitive profile information.

### 6. Retention

Hosting security records are retained according to the host’s operational schedule. Email correspondence is kept only as long as reasonably needed for the conversation, legal obligations and legitimate company records. A specific deletion request may be limited where retention is legally required.

### 7. Your choices

Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict or object to certain uses of personal information. You may also withdraw consent where consent is the basis of processing.

### 8. Contact

For a privacy question or request, write to hello@antigrav.si. Do not send identity documents unless we specifically confirm they are necessary and provide a secure route.

## Cookie & analytics policy

×

Last updated 30 October 2026Version 1.2

This policy explains every category of browser storage and measurement relevant to antigrav.si and what is active now.

Current status: Antigravity uses Simple Analytics, a privacy-first analytics service that sets no cookies and collects no personal data; it runs for all visitors. An advertising pixel from Meta is installed on this site but loads only after you accept in the cookie banner. No TikTok pixel is installed. Your banner choice is stored in your browser local storage so the site can honour it on later visits; no choice means no pixels.

### 1. What cookies are

Cookies are small text records a website or service can ask a browser to retain. Related technologies include local browser storage, software-development-kit identifiers, pixels and tags. They can support essential delivery, remember preferences, measure use or build advertising profiles. This policy uses “cookies” as a convenient term for these technologies unless a distinction matters.

### 2. What is active on this website

| Category | Status | Purpose and data | Duration |

| First-party essential cookies | Not set by this build | No account, sign-in, checkout or saved preference requires a cookie. | None |

| Audience analytics | Active (Simple Analytics) | Privacy-first page-view and anonymous event counts. No cookies, no personal data, no cross-site profile. Honors Do Not Track. | Aggregate only |

| Advertising | Active, consent only | The Meta Pixel loads only after you accept in the cookie banner. It measures page views, form submissions and booking clicks, and may build remarketing audiences on Meta. No TikTok pixel is installed. | Provider controlled |

| Site media | Active | Video and image files load from the site itself. Playback does not require a third-party player. | Request only |

| Google Fonts | Active | Font requests may expose ordinary connection data, including IP address, browser details and request time, to Google’s font delivery service. | Provider controlled |

| Hosting and security logs | Active | The host may process IP address, request path, time, user agent and diagnostic or security events to deliver and protect the site. | Host controlled |

| Error monitoring | Active | Sentry receives technical error reports from the browser: the error message, stack trace and browser metadata, so faults on this website can be found and fixed. It sets no cookies, records no sessions and is never used for measurement or advertising. | Provider controlled |

### 3. Analytics in use

Antigravity wants to understand whether the website communicates the company clearly. Simple Analytics measures aggregate page views only:

- page views, entry pages and broad referral source;

- coarse device, browser, language and country-level information.

That measurement would be used to improve narrative flow, reliability, accessibility and the effectiveness of company communications. It would not be used to read email contents, capture typed text, record a replay of the screen, collect precise location, or combine activity with an advertising profile.

### 4. Consent

Simple Analytics sets no cookies and collects no personal data, so it does not require consent under GDPR or ePrivacy rules and runs for all visitors. The Meta Pixel does require consent: it does not load until you accept in the cookie banner, the banner offers a decline option with equal prominence, and withdrawing consent is as straightforward as giving it. Reset my banner choice

shows the banner again so you can change your answer.

### 5. Retention and minimisation

Any future analytics configuration will collect the minimum fields needed for aggregate product decisions, use the shortest practical retention period, restrict access to people working on the website, and document the provider and exact duration in this table. Antigravity will avoid persistent identifiers where useful measurement can be achieved without them.

### 6. Third parties and international transfer

Simple Analytics and Google Fonts are the named external browser-delivered services. Their infrastructure may process requests in another country. Hosting and network providers may also route technical data internationally as part of ordinary internet delivery. Any additional analytics provider will be named here before activation.

### 7. Browser controls

You can block or delete cookies through browser settings. Blocking all cookies can affect websites that rely on sign-in or saved preferences, although this build of antigrav.si does not require them for its core content. Privacy extensions may also restrict external font requests.

### 8. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control

Simple Analytics is configured to honour Do Not Track (data-collect-dnt), so visits from browsers sending that signal are not counted. The Meta Pixel honours your banner choice: declining or resetting it stops the pixel loading on later visits.

### 9. First-party measurement principles

If Antigravity activates its own analytics, the system will be designed around purpose limitation. Events will be collected only to answer defined questions about whether the site is understandable, reliable and useful. The company will not collect data merely because a browser makes it technically possible. Event names, fields and retention periods will be reviewed before release and reduced when a less intrusive signal can answer the same question.

Where a consent requirement applies, analytics will remain inactive until consent is given. Declining analytics will not hide content, slow the site, disable contact information or reduce access to any public section.

### 10. Events a future setup could measure

None of these events is measured today. A future consent-based configuration may record an event when a visitor opens a major section, starts or pauses a film, follows a navigation control, opens a policy, copies an email address or selects an outbound email link. An event may include the event time, page version, broad device class, browser family, language, approximate country or region, referring-site category and a short-lived pseudonymous session identifier.

Antigravity does not intend to collect the text of messages, clipboard contents, keystrokes, form-field values, precise location, contact lists, installed applications, biometric information or a recording of the visitor’s screen. It will not deliberately create a fingerprint from fonts, hardware, canvas output or similar signals.

### 11. Information that will not be used for advertising

Analytics information collected for this site will not be used to select personalised advertisements, create a cross-site advertising audience, infer sensitive interests or sell a visitor profile. Antigravity will not ask an analytics provider to combine site activity with unrelated browsing history for ad targeting.

### 12. Consent records

If analytics is activated, Antigravity may need to retain a limited record showing that a consent choice was made. That record would contain the choice, the policy version, the time of the choice and a random preference identifier. It would not be used as an advertising identifier. The exact storage method and duration will be published here before use.

A visitor who withdraws consent will stop future optional measurement. Withdrawal does not automatically erase aggregate statistics already produced from earlier lawful processing, but a linked pseudonymous record will be deleted or de-identified where required and technically possible.

### 13. Purpose, legal basis and necessity

Essential network processing supports delivery, fraud prevention, availability and security. Optional audience analytics, if introduced, will rely on consent where consent is required by applicable law. In jurisdictions where another legal basis is available, Antigravity will still honour the controls described in the notice and will document any material difference in this policy.

### 14. Providers and access controls

Before any analytics provider is enabled, this policy will name the provider, describe its role, link to its relevant privacy information, identify whether it acts as a processor or independent controller, and state the configured retention period. Access to raw event data will be limited to authorised people working on this website, its security or company communications. Access will be reviewed and removed when no longer needed.

### 15. Aggregation, deletion and retention

Raw event-level records will be kept for the shortest practical period needed to validate collection, resolve errors and prepare aggregate reports. Longer-term reports should use totals, rates and trends rather than visitor-level histories. Deletion schedules will cover production data, routine backups and exports where technically feasible. A specific schedule will replace this general statement before optional analytics starts.

### 16. Security and incident response

Reasonable organisational and technical controls will be applied to analytics data, including access restriction, encryption in transit, service logging and vendor review. No internet service can promise absolute security. If an incident creates a legally reportable risk, Antigravity will follow applicable notification and remediation duties.

### 17. Children and sensitive information

This website is directed to business, technical, partnership and investment audiences and is not designed to profile children. Antigravity does not seek sensitive personal information through analytics. Visitors should not include medical, financial, government-identification or other sensitive information in an initial email.

### 18. Regional rights and complaints

Privacy rights vary by location and may include access, correction, deletion, portability, restriction, objection and withdrawal of consent. A request will be assessed under the law that applies to the requester and the processing. Antigravity may ask for proportionate verification before acting, but will not request more information than necessary to verify and complete the request.

If you believe a privacy concern has not been resolved, you may also have the right to contact the privacy or data-protection authority responsible for your region.

### 19. Changes to this policy

The version and date above will change when the categories, providers, purposes, controls or retention periods change. Material changes will be reflected in the notice shown on the site. Earlier policy versions may be retained for governance and legal records.

### 20. Questions

Questions about cookies, analytics or privacy can be sent to hello@antigrav.si. Please describe the nature of the request and the country or region relevant to it, but do not send identity documents or other sensitive records unless Antigravity confirms they are necessary and provides a secure route.

Mise is the back office that checks your invoices, your counts and your orders, in one place.

For quick-service restaurants, cafés & franchises across the United States and Canada

# See what’s running low before 4 PM on a Friday.

Mise is in its founding pilot, built by hand, kitchen by kitchen, with operators who want it to last. The 10-minute morning routine comes first: what could run out today, what yesterday cost you, the prep list, one order to approve.

Book a call See the 10-minute morning routine Or run the check yourself first: walk the demo Founding pilot · In development · Set up with you How it works

## The 10-minute morning routine.

Every morning at 08:15: what could run out today, what yesterday cost you, a two-minute stock count, the prep list and the opening checklist, one order to approve. Longer than ten minutes means something’s wrong.

Illustrated concept. Mise is in its founding pilot

Shelf truth from paper truth 08:15 BriefThe count: flagged items only

Food costs, explainedExplanations, not accusations

The CA$200 gateMise proposes. You approve.

### Count ten items. Not two hundred.

Mise flags only what needs eyes. Two minutes in the walk-in, then you’re done.

Soft cheese, bulk blockFlagged · order 2 Whole milkWatch · 1 day left Burger bunsWatch · Friday rush risk Chicken breast, portionedWatch · 2 days left Cheese slicesWatch · Friday rush risk Frying oilOK 12oz cupsOK Lettuce, shreddedOK Tomatoes, slicedOK Cola syrupOK

One item needs an order today. The rest can wait.

### Every number shows its work.

One tap shows the invoice photo, the count record, who entered it. Nobody gets blamed. The question is what happened, never who did it.

Opening9.6 kgFrom the count sheet. + Deliveries12.4 kgFrom checked invoices. − Recipe use7.8 kgFrom recipe cards. = Expected14.2 kgWorked out here. Counted11.8 kgFrom the ten item count. The gap−CA$12.60

The question is what happened, never who did it. Likely cause: unlogged batch waste. Next step: recount the walk-in before ordering.

Margins read off the same numbers: every dish set against the real cost of what went into it.

### You approve every order.

Mise drafts the order. If it’s over your CA$200 manager limit, it locks until the owner taps approve.

CA$248.00 On hold · awaiting owner

Changed the order? It needs your approval again. Nothing is ever ordered twice. You always sign off.

#### Without the check.

#### With the check.

Four steps set this up. None of them asks for a full count on day one. Setup, step by step

Proof · Measured by hand

## The invoices looked fine. Then Mise checked.

Before Mise was software, the check was done by hand, across a 15-location network. These are the manual pilot findings: what the checking did to the numbers, measured before the product existed. One checked month is kept below them as the exhibit.

The benchmark · 15 locations · Measured by hand 619invoice lines checked by hand, one by one $50,380.85in spend carried by those lines

| Measure | Before the check | After the check | Change |

| Billing errors | 8.72% | 0.18% | -8.54 pts |

| Price variance | 14.28% | 2.14% | -12.14 pts |

| Manager hours on the back office | 6.25 h | 1.75 h | -4.50 h |

Fifteen locations, one network, every line read against what was agreed and what arrived. Measured by hand, before Mise was software. The founding pilot is where the software has to match it.

Zone A · The exhibit · One checked month 515lines checked. Every invoice line in the month, read one by one. $42,012.65in spend checked, across those lines. $81.58average spend per line 30purchase dates in the month 24suppliers across the month Zone B · Where the money sat Dairy57.85% The two largest suppliers85.20%

Most of the money sat in few places. That is why every line got checked.

Zone C · One price, held flat

Milk, per 4L case, on all 35 lines from one supplier, across 29 dates.

Zone D · The method Step 1Read every line. Step 2Check it against what was agreed and what arrived. Step 3Write down what does not match.

Measured by hand, before Mise was software. The founding pilot is where the software has to match it.

And when a line does not match, it does not stop at a flag. The dispute goes to the supplier by email with the evidence pack attached: the flagged lines, the price that was agreed, and the receiving record. The supplier replies on the same thread, and the thread stays attached to the invoice.

Every result here has to fill every box. If a box is empty, the result does not go up.

Before After Period Locations Method Checked byHand or Software

Empty until a pilot result can fill every box.

Product screens

Everything in Mise

## The whole back office, in one place.

The morning brief is the part you open every day. Under it sits the whole back office: counts, invoices, orders, credits, waste, and the month-end books. Here is all of it.

The morning

- Morning briefThe day starts with one short brief: what might run out tonight, what yesterday cost you, and what needs a decision.

- Rush-risk warningsMise works out which items will not last through tonight’s rush, hour by hour, and puts them at the top of the brief.

- Store health scoreOne plain score in the brief shows how the store is doing today.

- Yesterday’s moneyEvery leak from yesterday is listed with its proof one tap away: the invoice, the count, and who entered it.

Counts and stock

- Guided countsA two-minute count of only the items Mise flags, zone by zone (walk-in, dry store, line), with cases, packs and loose units added up for you. You never do the math.

- Opening countBefore the first brief, an opening count sets the starting numbers, and you sign off the recipes, pack sizes and counts yourself.

- Count reviewWhere a count and the expected number disagree, you accept, split or correct the reason (used, wasted, overcharged, missing) before anything adjusts.

- Recipes and costingRecipes turn your sales into ingredient use. Each store can edit yields, sub-recipes and modifier rules like “extra bacon,” with costing kept up to date.

- Batch prepPrep batches are logged on the floor, and when sales pass a full batch, Mise records the next batch as made, so stock stays honest between counts.

- Expiring batchesBatches carry their shelf life, and the day’s expiring batches show on the floor pad before they become waste.

- Menu drift queueA new or changed item on your till that is not linked to ingredients raises a flag with a suggested link. Nothing slips past the stock math unlinked.

- Sunday spot-checkA short weekly check of the five highest-value items, so small losses surface before month end.

On the floor

- Floor PIN sessionsStaff open their own session with a Floor PIN and land on a floor pad with big tap targets, not the owner’s brief.

- Receiving checksAt the back door, staff check what arrived against what was ordered, while the truck is still there.

- Waste loggingWaste is logged in seconds on the pad, with who logged it, so yesterday’s money can show where food went.

- Panic-buy captureWhen something runs out mid-rush, the emergency buy is captured on the pad: a photo of the receipt, the amount, and which item ran out.

- Panic spend lineEmergency buys are priced against the wholesale price and reported as their own line, so you see exactly what running out costs.

- Food safety recordsTemperature and holding logs, batch shelf life and allergen records, kept as an evidence pack that is ready for inspection.

Invoices and suppliers

- Invoice checkingForward invoices by email or upload them. Mise reads them, flags duplicates and price changes, and checks every line three ways: against the order and against the delivery.

- Photo-side verificationAny line Mise is unsure of, including handwriting on a paper bill, opens side by side with the photo, so you confirm or fix it yourself. Nothing posts on a guess.

- Dispute draftsWhen an invoice is wrong, Mise drafts the dispute with the evidence attached, ready for you to send.

- Credits ledgerEvery promised supplier credit is tracked until the credit actually lands on a later invoice. A credit that never arrives stays open, aging where you can see it.

- Supplier catalogueYour supplier list builds itself from your invoices: pack sizes, prices, and who supplies what.

- Shrinking packsIf a supplier quietly shrinks a pack, the cost per unit gives it away, and the change is flagged.

Orders

- One proposed orderOne order, worked out from your stock, expected demand, delivery days, pack sizes and prices, with its reason in one plain sentence.

- Approval of exact contentsNothing is ever sent without your yes on the exact contents. Change anything and it needs a fresh yes. Retries never send an order twice.

- Minimums and cutoffsSupplier minimums and order cutoffs count down on the approval screen, with a reminder before a cutoff is missed.

- Unacknowledged ordersIf a supplier does not confirm an order in time, the order shows it, with the next step named (call, or send it elsewhere). Never silent waiting.

The books

- Savings ledgerA running ledger of what Mise has caught and corrected for the store, month by month, in plain dollars.

- Month-end packAt month end, every movement traces back to its evidence, ready for your accountant. Mise is not your accounting system; it hands over a clean pack.

- Delivery-platform checksMonthly statements from the delivery apps are checked line by line (sales, minus the platform’s cut, minus refund clawbacks), and fault-waste claims are tracked until they land.

- Availability adviceIf an item runs out, Mise advises pausing it on the delivery apps. It never pauses anything on its own.

Repairs and creative help

- Facilities marketplaceWhen equipment breaks, hire vetted local trades from listings that show their papers in the open. You pay the provider directly; Mise keeps the booking and the record, and never touches the money.

- Creative marketplaceVideographers, photographers and menu designers, hired the same way: papers in the open, paid directly by you, and every campaign’s spend approved by you first.

Anywhere

- Works offlineCounts and logs keep working with no connection, saved safely on the device, and send when the connection returns. Nothing is lost, and nothing is doubled.

- Honest connection statesIf a connection breaks, the screen says so, says when it last worked, and marks anything waiting as queued, never as sent.

- Web, phone and tabletThe same Mise on the web, iPhone, iPad and Android, in light or dark, with controls that stay easy to tap.

- Roles and assigned storesOwners, managers and floor staff each sign in with their own role and see their own stores.

Setup

## Set up with you, in four steps.

You work long days, so setup happens in steps, at your pace. Your store enters its own data with our tooling, and we walk through it together until each step holds. Nothing is entered for you, and nothing starts until the numbers are yours.

STEP 01

#### Connect your POS

You giveYour authorisation, inside Clover on a call together: one tap grants Mise read only access to your account. Nobody hands over a login. Mise doesConnects through that authorisation, read only, and sets your manager limit. Any order over CA$200 waits for the owner. Your timeAbout 10 minutes. Done whenYour sales show in Mise the same day. STEP 02

#### Your recipes, as a starting point

You giveThe recipe each dish started with, as it stands today. Mise doesLoads them as the measure. Cooks adjust on the line; Mise measures against your original, not a guess. Your timeAbout 20 minutes for a standard menu. Done whenEvery dish has a starting recipe on record. STEP 03

#### Enter your stock, with us beside you

You giveYour item list, from your shelves and your invoices. Mise doesProvides the tooling and stays on the call while you enter each item, so every item lands the way your kitchen names it. Your timeOne sitting, about 30 to 45 minutes for most kitchens. Done whenYour stock list matches what is on your shelves. STEP 04

#### Count when it suits you

You giveA first ten item count, whenever it suits. Mise doesStarts the morning briefs from your count. No full count on day one. Your timeTwo minutes, in the walk-in. Done whenYour first 08:15 brief arrives the next morning.

All of it is gatherable in one shift.

Your suppliers stay yours. Your recipes stay yours. Your team keeps ordering the way they do today until the brief replaces the guesswork. And nothing is ever ordered without a person approving it.

The marketplace

## Services you can trust.

Mise is also a marketplace. When the fridge breaks at 4 PM, or the menu needs a camera, you hire from listings that show their papers in the open. No badges. No claim the documents do not support.

#### Repairs and servicing

Refrigeration, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, pest control: the trades a store runs on. Every listing shows the documents behind it, each with its expiry date: insurance, licence, registration. A document close to expiry shows as close to expiry. A missing document shows as missing.

#### Creative

Videographers, photographers, menu designers. The same rule as the trades: the work sits in the open, the papers sit beside it, and the listing says plainly what is on file and what is not.

Questions

## Asked in the order they block the call.

What does setup ask of me?

Four steps, at your pace. You enter your own data with our tooling, walked through together. The minimum to start fits in one shift: your Clover authorisation (read only, granted by you on the call), one recent supplier invoice, your recipes as they stand, and a time for a first count. Does it work with my POS?

Clover connects today. Other systems are in pilot or not yet, and the fit check above gives the plain answer for yours. If yours is not live, the waitlist writes to you the day it opens. No date is promised. Is it finished?

No, and we would rather say so. Mise is in its founding pilot, set up store by store. The first value is not the finished product. It is the invoice check on the call, run on one of your own invoices. What does it cost?

Pricing is per location, and it is explained whole on the 15-minute call, in your own invoice numbers: what it costs, what it has to save, and the terms, in the same order for every store at the same stage. In Canada the terms are in Canadian dollars; in the United States, in US dollars. Nothing is charged on this page, and no card is taken here. How does the trial work?

The pilot opens with a 14-day trial. A card is saved when the trial starts and is charged only when the trial ends, and you get a warning three days before the first charge. The data rights terms land in writing before the trial starts, so nothing about the card or your records is a surprise. What if it does not save more than it costs?

On day 30 you get a written proof report on your own records, worked against the baseline set in the first checked week of your pilot: what was checked, what was found, what it saved. There is no guarantee and there are no refunds. We would rather you judge the report than a promise. What happens to my data?

The details you send in the form are used to answer your request and run your pilot, and nothing else. Your store’s records stay yours. The data rights terms are given in writing before any trial starts, and before a card is saved, so you can read them before anything begins. Support, when you ask for it, sees what the owner sees and changes nothing: access is read only, agreed with you, and time-boxed, and emergency access is declared to the owner at the moment it happens. Every company that touches your invoices is named in those terms, including the service that reads them.

One more thing decides most calls: the biggest problem field in the form below. Book a call

Leaving

## Leaving is as plain as joining.

Cancelling is exactly as easy as signing up. There is no retention maze and no call you have to sit through to leave. Fees are non-refundable, and that is stated in the contract before you sign. Your records on exit stay yours and stay exportable for twelve months after you leave, with a warning before anything is deleted. Come back inside the year and everything is restored exactly as you left it. Coming back is on the intro terms of the day you return, never a worse rung for having left. Founding terms are not promised on a return; they belong to the cohort that stayed. Marketing emails end with one click or one reply. The words are the same in every footer: unsubscribe at any time.

Mise est l’arrière-boutique qui vérifie vos factures, vos comptages et vos commandes, au même endroit.

Pour les restaurants rapides, les cafés et les franchises aux États-Unis et au Canada

# Voyez ce qui va manquer avant 16 h, le vendredi.

Mise est en pilote fondateur, bâti à la main, cuisine par cuisine, avec des exploitants qui veulent que ça dure. La routine matinale de 10 minutes vient en premier : ce qui pourrait manquer aujourd’hui, ce qu’hier vous a coûté, la liste de préparation, une commande à approuver.

Réserver un appel Voir la routine matinale de 10 minutes Ou faites la vérification vous-même d’abord : parcourez la démo Pilote fondateur · En développement · Installation avec vous Fonctionnement

## La routine matinale de 10 minutes.

Chaque matin à 8 h 15 : ce qui pourrait manquer aujourd’hui, ce qu’hier vous a coûté, un comptage de deux minutes, la liste de préparation et la liste d’ouverture, une commande à approuver. Plus de dix minutes, c’est qu’il y a un problème.

Concept illustré. Mise est en pilote fondateur

La vérité des tablettes vient de la vérité du papier 8 h 15 · BriefLe comptage : les articles signalés seulement

Les coûts, expliquésDes explications, pas des accusations

Le seuil de 200 $Mise propose. Vous approuvez.

### Comptez dix articles. Pas deux cents.

Mise signale seulement ce qui a besoin d’un œil. Deux minutes dans la chambre froide, et c’est terminé.

Fromage mou, bloc en vracSignalé · en commander 2 Lait entierÀ surveiller · 1 jour restant Pains à hamburgerÀ surveiller · risque au rush du vendredi Poitrines de poulet, portionnéesÀ surveiller · 2 jours restants Fromage en tranchesÀ surveiller · risque au rush du vendredi Huile à fritureOK Verres 12 ozOK Laitue, émincéeOK Tomates, tranchéesOK Sirop de colaOK

Un article a besoin d’une commande aujourd’hui. Le reste peut attendre.

### Chaque chiffre montre son calcul.

Un toucher montre la photo de la facture, le registre du comptage, qui l’a entré. Personne n’est blâmé. La question est ce qui s’est passé, jamais qui l’a fait.

Ouverture9,6 kgDe la feuille de comptage. + Livraisons12,4 kgDes factures vérifiées. − Usage des recettes7,8 kgDes fiches de recettes. = Attendu14,2 kgCalculé ici. Compté11,8 kgDu comptage de dix articles. L’écart−12,60 $

La question est ce qui s’est passé, jamais qui l’a fait. Cause probable : un gaspillage de lot non consigné. Prochaine étape : recompter la chambre froide avant de commander.

Les marges se lisent sur les mêmes chiffres : chaque plat comparé au coût réel de ce qui est entré dedans.

### Vous approuvez chaque commande.

Mise prépare la commande. Si elle dépasse votre limite de gestionnaire de 200 $, elle se verrouille jusqu’à ce que le propriétaire approuve.

248,00 $ En attente · du propriétaire

Vous avez modifié la commande ? Elle a besoin de votre approbation à nouveau. Rien n’est jamais commandé deux fois. C’est toujours vous qui approuvez.

#### Sans la vérification.

8 h 15Aucun brief. La journée commence à l’aveugle. MidiLa facture est classée, non vérifiée. Après-midiLa commande est écrite de mémoire. 16 hUne case de tablette est vide, au moment où le rush commence. Journée type

#### Avec la vérification.

8 h 15La carte du brief : trois articles à surveiller. MidiLait entier, boîte de 4 L Signalé Après-midiLa feuille de comptage : dix lignes, faites en deux minutes. 16 hLa tablette est pleine. La feuille de commande indique Approuvé. Journée type

Quatre étapes installent le tout. Aucune ne demande un comptage complet le premier jour. L’installation, étape par étape

Preuve · Mesuré à la main

## Les factures semblaient correctes. Puis Mise a vérifié.

Avant que Mise soit un logiciel, la vérification se faisait à la main, dans un réseau de 15 emplacements. Voici les résultats du pilote manuel : ce que la vérification a fait aux chiffres, mesuré avant que le produit existe. Un mois vérifié est conservé ci-dessous comme pièce à l’appui.

Le repère · 15 emplacements · Mesuré à la main 619lignes de facture vérifiées à la main, une par une 50 380,85 $de dépenses portées par ces lignes

| Mesure | Avant la vérification | Après la vérification | Écart |

| Erreurs de facturation | 8,72 % | 0,18 % | -8,54 pts |

| Écart de prix | 14,28 % | 2,14 % | -12,14 pts |

| Heures de gestion au bureau arrière | 6,25 h | 1,75 h | -4,50 h |

Quinze emplacements, un seul réseau, chaque ligne lue contre ce qui avait été convenu et ce qui était arrivé. Mesuré à la main, avant que Mise soit un logiciel. Le pilote fondateur est l’endroit où le logiciel doit égaler ce résultat.

Zone A · La pièce à l’appui · Un mois vérifié 515lignes vérifiées. Chaque ligne de facture du mois, lue une par une. 42 012,65 $de dépenses vérifiées, sur ces lignes. 81,58 $dépense moyenne par ligne 30dates d’achat dans le mois 24fournisseurs dans le mois Zone B · Où l’argent se trouvait Produits laitiers57,85 % Les deux plus gros fournisseurs85,20 %

La plus grande partie de l’argent se trouvait à peu d’endroits. C’est pourquoi chaque ligne a été vérifiée.

Zone C · Un prix, resté fixe

Le lait, par boîte de 4 L, sur les 35 lignes d’un seul fournisseur, sur 29 dates.

Zone D · La méthode Étape 1Lire chaque ligne. Étape 2La vérifier contre ce qui avait été convenu et ce qui était arrivé. Étape 3Consigner ce qui ne correspond pas.

Mesuré à la main, avant que Mise soit un logiciel. Le pilote fondateur, c’est là où le logiciel doit arriver au même niveau.

Et quand une ligne ne correspond pas, ça ne s’arrête pas à un signalement. Le litige part au fournisseur par courriel avec le dossier de preuve joint : les lignes signalées, le prix qui avait été convenu et le registre de réception. Le fournisseur répond sur le même fil, et le fil reste attaché à la facture.

Chaque résultat ici doit remplir chaque case. Si une case est vide, le résultat n’est pas publié.

Avant Après Période Emplacements Méthode Vérifié parÀ la main ou logiciel

Vide jusqu’à ce qu’un résultat de pilote puisse remplir chaque case.

Installation

## Installé avec vous, en quatre étapes.

Vous travaillez de longues journées, alors l’installation se fait par étapes, à votre rythme. Votre commerce entre ses propres données avec nos outils, et nous parcourons chaque étape ensemble jusqu’à ce qu’elle tienne. Rien n’est entré pour vous, et rien ne commence avant que les chiffres soient les vôtres.

ÉTAPE 01

#### Connectez votre point de vente

Vous donnezVotre autorisation, dans Clover lors d’un appel ensemble : un toucher accorde à Mise un accès en lecture seule à votre compte. Aucun identifiant n’est partagé. Mise faitSe connecte par cette autorisation, en lecture seule, et règle votre limite de gestionnaire. Toute commande de plus de 200 $ attend le propriétaire. Votre tempsEnviron 10 minutes. Terminé quandVos ventes apparaissent dans Mise le jour même. ÉTAPE 02

#### Vos recettes, comme point de départ

Vous donnezLa recette de départ de chaque plat, telle qu’elle est aujourd’hui. Mise faitLes charge comme mesure. Les cuisiniers ajustent sur la ligne; Mise mesure contre votre original, pas contre une devinette. Votre tempsEnviron 20 minutes pour un menu standard. Terminé quandChaque plat a une recette de départ au dossier. ÉTAPE 03

#### Entrez votre stock, avec nous à vos côtés

Vous donnezVotre liste d’articles, de vos tablettes et de vos factures. Mise faitFournit les outils et reste à l’appel pendant que vous entrez chaque article, pour que chaque article porte le nom que votre cuisine lui donne. Votre tempsUne séance, environ 30 à 45 minutes pour la plupart des cuisines. Terminé quandVotre liste de stock correspond à ce qui est sur vos tablettes. ÉTAPE 04

#### Comptez quand ça vous convient

Vous donnezUn premier comptage de dix articles, quand ça vous convient. Mise faitDémarre les briefs du matin à partir de votre comptage. Aucun comptage complet le premier jour. Votre tempsDeux minutes, dans la chambre froide. Terminé quandVotre premier brief de 8 h 15 arrive le lendemain matin.

#### À avoir prêt avant la première étape

- Votre compte Clover, pour autoriser l’accès en lecture seule pendant l’appel.

- Une facture fournisseur récente.

- Vos recettes, telles qu’elles sont.

- Un moment pour un premier comptage, n’importe quand dans la première semaine.

Tout se rassemble en un seul quart de travail.

#### Ce qui ne change pas

Vos fournisseurs restent les vôtres. Vos recettes restent les vôtres. Votre équipe continue de commander comme aujourd’hui jusqu’à ce que le brief remplace les devinettes. Et rien n’est jamais commandé sans l’approbation d’une personne.

#### Inclus dans le pilote fondateur

- Comptages

- Vérification des factures

- Approbation des commandes

- Le brief du matin

- L’installation, parcourue ensemble

#### Pas encore

Les intégrations au-delà des systèmes nommés dans la vérification d’adéquation ci-dessous ne font pas partie du pilote. Nommés franchement comme étapes ultérieures : la place de marché, les listes de préparation et d’ouverture, et les vues de marges. Tout ce qui n’est pas nommé comme inclus est une étape ultérieure, et nous le dirons franchement plutôt que de vous laisser supposer.

La première étape est un appel de 15 minutes. Vérifiez d’abord votre adéquation

La place de marché

## Des services de confiance.

Mise est aussi une place de marché. Quand le frigo lâche à 16 h, ou que le menu a besoin d’une caméra, vous embauchez à partir d’annonces qui montrent leurs papiers au grand jour. Aucun badge. Aucune affirmation que les documents ne soutiennent pas.

#### Réparations et entretien

Réfrigération, chauffage, ventilation et climatisation, plomberie, électricité, nettoyage, lutte antiparasitaire : les métiers qui font tourner un commerce. Chaque annonce montre les documents derrière elle, chacun avec sa date d’expiration : assurance, permis, enregistrement. Un document proche de l’expiration paraît proche de l’expiration. Un document manquant paraît manquant.

#### Créatif

Vidéastes, photographes, concepteurs de menus. La même règle que les métiers : le travail est au grand jour, les papiers sont à côté, et l’annonce dit franchement ce qui est au dossier et ce qui ne l’est pas.

Réfrigération · Votre villeNouveau fournisseur · Aucun travail encore Certificat d’assuranceAu dossier · Expiration affichée Permis de métierAu dossier · Expiration affichée Enregistrement d’entrepriseManquant · Affiché comme manquant

Annonce type, montrée comme toutes les annonces se montrent. Aucune évaluation : les évaluations attendent de vrais travaux. Les commerces paient les fournisseurs directement. Mise ne touche jamais à l’argent.

#### Vous exercez un métier, ou tenez une caméra ?

Faites-vous trouver par les entreprises alimentaires près de chez vous. Inscription gratuite. Les commerces vous paient directement. La place de marché ouvre par étapes, après l’arrière-boutique du pilote fondateur. Laissez vos coordonnées dans le formulaire ci-dessous et dites que vous êtes un fournisseur : votre métier ou votre art, votre ville, et ce que vous faites. Nous écrirons quand votre catégorie ouvrira. Aucun travail n’est promis.

Inscrire mon intérêt comme fournisseur

La visite guidée

## Faites la vérification de vos propres mains.

La démo, c’est la routine, sur un commerce d’exemple. Quatre étapes, dans l’ordre où le produit les exécute. C’est une visite guidée, pas un essai : aucun compte, aucune carte, rien à installer.

Commerce d’exemple · Une cuisine de restauration rapide

ÉTAPE 1

#### Le brief du matin

Voyez la journée comme l’exploitant la voit à 8 h 15.

ÉTAPE 2

#### Le comptage de dix articles

Comptez dix articles sur un téléphone, par-dessus la feuille de comptage.

ÉTAPE 3

#### La vérification de facture

Trois vérifications sur une facture : le prix contre ce qui avait été convenu, la livraison contre ce qui avait été commandé, et le calcul des lignes.

ÉTAPE 4

#### L’approbation de la commande

Approuvez la commande vous-même. Rien ne bouge sans une personne.

Une ligne, suivie de la facture à la tablette Commencer la visite guidée

Si la visite guidée ne s’ouvre pas, ou charge une page blanche, ne vous battez pas avec. Réservez l’appel et nous faisons la même vérification en direct, sur une de vos factures.

L’appel fait la même vérification sur une de vos propres factures.

Réserver un appel Continuer à regarder

Si vous réservez après avoir parcouru la démo, votre demande le note, et l’appel commence à la même vérification.

Questions

## Posées dans l’ordre où elles bloquent l’appel.

Qu’est-ce que l’installation me demande ?

Quatre étapes, à votre rythme. Vous entrez vos propres données avec nos outils, parcourues ensemble. Le minimum pour commencer tient en un quart de travail : votre autorisation Clover, en lecture seule et accordée par vous pendant l’appel, une facture fournisseur récente, vos recettes telles qu’elles sont, et un moment pour un premier comptage. Est-ce que ça fonctionne avec mon point de vente ?

Clover se connecte aujourd’hui. Les autres systèmes sont en pilote ou pas encore, et la vérification d’adéquation ci-dessus donne la réponse franche pour le vôtre. Si le vôtre n’est pas en service, la liste d’attente vous écrit le jour où ça ouvre. Aucune date n’est promise. Est-ce que c’est terminé ?

Non, et nous préférons le dire. Mise est en pilote fondateur, installé commerce par commerce. La première valeur n’est pas le produit fini. C’est la vérification de facture à l’appel, faite sur une de vos propres factures. Combien ça coûte ?

Le prix est par emplacement, et il est expliqué au complet à l’appel de 15 minutes, dans les chiffres de vos propres factures : ce que ça coûte, ce que ça doit économiser, et les conditions, dans le même ordre pour chaque commerce au même stade. Au Canada, les conditions sont en dollars canadiens; aux États-Unis, en dollars américains. Rien n’est facturé sur cette page, et aucune carte n’y est prise. Comment fonctionne l’essai ?

Le pilote s’ouvre avec un essai de 14 jours. Une carte est enregistrée au début de l’essai et n’est débitée qu’à la fin de l’essai, et vous recevez un avertissement trois jours avant le premier débit. Les conditions sur les droits de données arrivent par écrit avant le début de l’essai, pour que rien, ni la carte ni vos dossiers, ne soit une surprise. Et si ça n’économise pas plus que ça coûte ?

Au jour 30, vous recevez un rapport de preuve écrit sur vos propres dossiers, travaillé contre la base fixée dans la première semaine vérifiée de votre pilote : ce qui a été vérifié, ce qui a été trouvé, ce qui a été économisé. Il n’y a aucune garantie et aucun remboursement. Nous préférons que vous jugiez le rapport plutôt qu’une promesse. Qu’arrive-t-il à mes données ?

Les détails que vous envoyez dans le formulaire servent à répondre à votre demande et à faire fonctionner votre pilote, et à rien d’autre. Les dossiers de votre commerce restent les vôtres. Les conditions sur les droits de données sont données par écrit avant le début de tout essai, et avant qu’une carte soit enregistrée, pour que vous puissiez les lire avant que quoi que ce soit commence. Le soutien, quand vous le demandez, voit ce que le propriétaire voit et ne change rien : l’accès est en lecture seule, convenu avec vous et limité dans le temps, et tout accès d’urgence est déclaré au propriétaire au moment même où il se produit. Chaque entreprise qui touche vos factures est nommée dans ces conditions, y compris le service qui les lit.

Une chose de plus décide la plupart des appels : le champ du plus gros problème dans le formulaire ci-dessous. Réserver un appel

Le départ

## Partir est aussi simple que se joindre.

L’annulation est exactement aussi facile que s’inscrire. Il n’y a aucun labyrinthe de rétention et aucun appel à endurer pour partir. Les frais sont non remboursables, et c’est énoncé dans le contrat avant que vous le signiez. Vos dossiers au départ restent les vôtres et restent exportables pendant douze mois après votre départ, avec un avertissement avant toute suppression. Revenez dans l’année et tout est restauré exactement comme vous l’aviez laissé. Le retour se fait aux conditions d’introduction du jour de votre retour, jamais un échelon pire pour être parti. Les conditions fondatrices ne sont pas promises lors d’un retour; elles appartiennent à la cohorte qui est restée. Les courriels de marketing prennent fin avec un clic ou une réponse. Les mots sont les mêmes dans chaque pied de page : se désabonner en tout temps.

# Partner with Antigravity.

Intelligence for physical work, kitchens first, one brain across kitchens, construction, and mechanics.

We are interested in building the physical step with the right partner. If you build bodies, sensors, or the hardware real work runs on, we want to talk.

Start a conversationSee the plan

Who we want to talk to

## Five kinds of partner.

01 / The body step

### Mechatronics and robotics

What it could look likeYour body, our brain in training. We bring real operations and the record of how work is done, and we test together in the trades we already serve.

02 / The capture layer

### IoT, sensors, wearables, cameras

What it could look likeYour hardware inside real operations, placed through a service businesses already use, capturing the work with consent.

03 / Proving grounds

### Operators and groups

What it could look likeYour kitchens, sites, or shops as the real places where the service runs today and the next steps get proven.

04 / The data

### Technical and research partners

What it could look likeShared work on physical work data: one format across trades, honest comparison with public data, and small, measured experiments.

05 / The setting

### Institutions

What it could look likeProgrammes and institutions working where software meets real-world execution, from pilots to standards.

# Privacy

Last updated 30 October 2026Website privacy noticeVersion 1.2

This notice explains what happens to information when you visit this website or contact Antigravity Analytics Private Limited.

## 1. Who is responsible

Antigravity Analytics Private Limited is responsible for the information it receives through this website and through messages sent to its published email addresses.

## 2. Information involved

- Technical delivery data: IP address, browser and device details, request time, requested file, referring page and basic security logs may be processed by the site host to deliver and protect the website.

- Correspondence: if you email us, we receive the address you use, the contents of your message and any attachments you choose to send.

- Website preferences: this build does not create a first-party account, profile or persistent preference record.

## 3. Why information is used

Technical data is used to deliver the site, maintain security, diagnose faults and understand aggregate demand. Correspondence is used to answer the purpose of your message, evaluate a partnership or investment conversation, and keep a necessary business record.

## 4. Analytics programme

Antigravity uses Simple Analytics to understand aggregate page views, broad traffic sources and anonymous interaction events (section views, button and link clicks). The purpose is to improve the clarity, accessibility and reliability of the site, not to build advertising profiles. Simple Analytics sets no cookies, collects no personal data, and honours Do Not Track.

Advertising measurement is also present, and it runs only with your consent. If you accept in the cookie banner, the Meta Pixel loads on this site. It records page views, form submissions and booking link clicks, sets cookies, and shares device, browser and interaction data with Meta so Antigravity can measure campaign performance and show ads to people who visited this site. If you decline, the pixel does not load and nothing is sent to Meta by this site. No TikTok pixel is installed on this site. Your choice is stored in your browser local storage, and you can change it at any time from the Cookies section of this page. Advertising measurement will not capture message contents, keystrokes, clipboard contents, precise location, identity documents, sensitive attributes or screen recordings.

## 5. Sharing

Information may be handled by infrastructure and email providers acting for Antigravity, or disclosed where required by law. It is not sold as a personal-data list. We do not use this website to collect payment-card details, government identifiers or sensitive profile information.

## 6. Retention

Hosting security records are retained according to the host’s operational schedule. Email correspondence is kept only as long as reasonably needed for the conversation, legal obligations and legitimate company records. A specific deletion request may be limited where retention is legally required.

## 7. Your choices

Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict or object to certain uses of personal information. You may also withdraw consent where consent is the basis of processing.

## 8. Contact

For a privacy question or request, write to hello@antigrav.si. Do not send identity documents unless we specifically confirm they are necessary and provide a secure route.
